solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Sends out one’s appeals (6)

blocks.note: to sue is to appeal or plead, as in suing for peace

annotation.surface: Someone mails off their own charity appeals.
annotation.walkthrough: 'One’s' is read literally: the numeral I followed by its apostrophe-S.
annotation.definitionFit: A publisher issues, or sends out, a statement or a stamp.

entries.clue: Small instrument out of tune (5)

blocks.note: standard abbreviation, as on clothing labels

annotation.surface: A little instrument that won't stay in tune.
annotation.walkthrough: A note played sharp is pitched too high, so it is out of tune.
annotation.definitionFit: Sharp describes a note pitched above where it should be, hence out of tune.

entries.clue: Not affected by exhausted urchin feeding in frenzy (9)

indicators.note: an exhausted word has been emptied of its insides, leaving only its outer letters
letters in a frenzy are thrown into wild disorder

blocks.note: URCHIN emptied of its middle leaves U…N

annotation.surface: A tired street child falls on food in a frenzy, with no pretence about it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Exhausted' looks like the urchin's tiredness; it is an instruction to empty the word, leaving only its first and last letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Unfeigned means genuine, not put on, so not affected.

entries.clue: Austere European novelist (6)

annotation.surface: A description of a severe continental writer.
annotation.walkthrough: Laurence Sterne wrote Tristram Shandy; the surface reads as one adjective-laden description of a single writer.
annotation.definitionFit: Laurence Sterne was an eighteenth-century novelist.

entries.clue: Strong defence of royal assistant from reporter (8)

indicators.note: a reporter speaks the words, so we hear their sound rather than their spelling

annotation.surface: A journalist gets a staunch defence of a royal aide.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Reporter' sounds like a newspaper story about the palace; it is the signal that the words are to be heard.
annotation.definitionFit: A palisade is a fence of stakes built as a defensive barrier.

entries.clue: In sporting contest a cramp simply worsens with age (10,5)

indicators.note: letters that worsen are knocked out of shape, so rearranged

annotation.surface: An ageing athlete finds a cramp only gets worse over the years.
annotation.walkthrough: The Paralympic Games are for disabled athletes, which gives the surface about bodily ailments a fitting edge. 'Age' sits apart from the other fodder but joins it.
annotation.definitionFit: The Paralympic Games are an international multi-sport contest.

entries.clue: Be keen to pass on writing with pen (8)

blocks.note: to long for something is to be keen on it
to hand something on is to pass it

annotation.surface: Someone eager to give up handwriting.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pass on' reads as declining; here it means handing something over.
annotation.definitionFit: Longhand is ordinary writing done by hand, with a pen, rather than typed or in shorthand.

entries.clue: Jostling crowd’s right to enter film (5)

indicators.note: the R goes into the other word

blocks.note: scum is a film on the surface of a liquid

annotation.surface: A pushing mob has the right to get into a cinema showing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Film' suggests a movie; it is a thin layer on a pond.
annotation.definitionFit: A scrum is a disorderly crowd of people pushing against each other.

entries.clue: Girl presented risk, squandering initial security (9)

indicators.note: to squander the initial is to throw away the first letter

blocks.note: a deb (debutante) is a girl presented at court or in society
VENTURE (a risk) without its first letter

annotation.surface: A young woman took a gamble and lost her early safety net.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Security' closes the surface as safety; it is the financial kind, a bond.
annotation.definitionFit: A debenture is a loan bond, one of the financial instruments called securities.

entries.clue: Appliance for cooking tough rabbit heads (6,4)

indicators.note: rabbit heads tough: it goes in front of it

blocks.note: to rabbit (on) is British slang for talking at length, as is to waffle
iron = tough, as in an iron will

annotation.surface: A gadget to cook rabbits' heads that are tough.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rabbit' is a verb here, not the animal: British slang for chattering, which is also what 'waffle' means. 'Heads' tells you it comes first.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain description: a hinged, gridded pair of hot plates that cooks batter into waffles.

entries.clue: Stone arguably regularly deficient (4)

indicators.note: the word is short of every other letter, at regular intervals

annotation.surface: A gem that, you could argue, is routinely flawed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Arguably' seems to hedge the surface's claim; it is the source word, losing alternate letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a red gemstone, one of the precious stones.

entries.clue: Voluntary work, a lot in labouring (8)

indicators.note: letters labouring are worked over, knocked into a new shape

annotation.surface: Unpaid work, and much of it is hard labour.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Voluntary work' reads as one phrase; the definition is only 'Voluntary', and 'work' starts the wordplay. 'In' is fodder, not a link.
annotation.definitionFit: Something optional is voluntary, left to choice.

entries.clue: One of us English showing compassion (6)

blocks.note: each of us is a human

annotation.surface: An Englishman, one of our own, being kind.
annotation.walkthrough: 'One of us' reads as a member of the group; it is simply a person, any member of the species.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: kind and merciful towards others, as in humane treatment.

entries.clue: Prime minister of northern country forgetting first two points (4)

indicators.note: the first two letters are forgotten, dropped

blocks.clueFragment: northern country forgetting first two points
blocks.note: SWEDEN loses S and W, two compass points

annotation.surface: A Scandinavian leader who has lost two points.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Points' are compass points, and S and W happen to be the first two letters of SWEDEN.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Anthony, who led the British government in 1955–57 and resigned over Suez.

entries.clue: Name ships in book (9)

annotation.surface: A list of ships' names appears in a book.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like it places the ships inside the book; it only links the wordplay to the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Dubliners is James Joyce's book of short stories.

entries.clue: Fabulous creature’s alien character grasped by child (8)

indicators.note: the character is held inside the child

blocks.note: a minor is a child in law
tau is a Greek letter, a foreign character

annotation.surface: A little one clutches the strange personality of a mythical beast.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Character' reads as personality; it is a letter of an alphabet, and 'alien' makes it a foreign one.
annotation.definitionFit: The Minotaur is a creature of Greek myth, half man and half bull.

entries.clue: Realised line may achieve the same as doing this? (6-3)

definitions.text: may achieve the same as doing this?

blocks.note: to tumble to something is to realise it

annotation.surface: A puzzle about whether a line achieves what doing something else does.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Line' does double duty: the railway in the wordplay, and the washing line in the definition, which dries clothes just as tumble-drying does.
annotation.definitionFit: A washing line dries clothes, achieving the same as tumble-drying them.

entries.clue: Lion, say, caught in a desert, falls (8)

indicators.note: C sits inside the other word

blocks.note: a lion is an example of a cat

annotation.surface: A lion is captured in the desert and topples.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Desert' looks like sand; it is a verb, to rat on someone. 'Falls' likewise is the noun, a waterfall.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a large steep waterfall; 'falls' is the noun, not the verb.

entries.clue: City companion wearing a short outfit (3,5)

indicators.note: the companion wears the outfit, so sits inside it
the outfit is cut short, losing its last letter

blocks.note: HABIT (an outfit, as a nun's) cut short

annotation.surface: A friend in a skimpy costume in town.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Short outfit' pictures a mini-skirt; it is a habit docked a letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Abu Dhabi is the capital city of the United Arab Emirates.

entries.clue: Easily cowed, I’m alarmed by motorway (4)

indicators.note: the cry is placed beside the motorway, which comes first

blocks.note: M, as in the M1 motorway
eek! is a cry of alarm

annotation.surface: A nervous driver is frightened by the motorway.
annotation.walkthrough: British motorways are numbered M1, M25 and so on, so M stands for motorway.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: quiet, submissive and quick to give way.

entries.clue: Promise extreme hardship (6)

blocks.note: an old verb for pledge, surviving in the wedding vow to ___ one's troth
a dire situation, as in the ___ of refugees

annotation.surface: A vow made in dire straits.
annotation.walkthrough: The verb sense survives mainly in 'plight one's troth', the old wedding vow.
annotation.definitionFit: Plight means both to pledge and a grave predicament.

entries.clue: Dog that is mainly East European (6)

indicators.note: only the main part of the word, dropping its last letter

annotation.surface: A dog that mostly comes from Eastern Europe.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is literally true: the vizsla is a Hungarian breed.
annotation.definitionFit: The vizsla is a Hungarian breed of pointing dog.

entries.clue: Dresser generally holds material (5)

indicators.note: the phrase holds the answer within it

annotation.surface: A sideboard usually has cloth in it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dresser' pictures kitchen furniture or a person who dresses; either way it is only a container of letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Serge is a hard-wearing twilled fabric.

entries.clue: I depend on girl related to astronomer (8)

indicators.note: in a down or across entry, one thing on another comes after it

blocks.note: to lean on is to depend on

annotation.surface: A dependent daughter linked to a stargazer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Depend on' reads as a phrase; here 'on' is split off to put I LEAN after the girl.
annotation.definitionFit: Galilean means relating to Galileo, the astronomer.

entries.clue: Coffee substitute that comes in a cup (5)

blocks.note: an oak's nut, roasted and ground, was brewed in wartime in place of coffee
the oak's nut grows in a scaly cup, the cupule

annotation.surface: An ersatz coffee served in a cup.
annotation.walkthrough: The cup is not a coffee cup but the scaly cupule an acorn grows in.
annotation.definitionFit: Acorn coffee was a wartime substitute, and each acorn sits in a cup.

entries.clue: Good feeling for music equipment (4)

blocks.note: an ear for music is a feel for it

annotation.surface: A fine sense of music for hi-fi kit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'For music' belongs to the ear phrase; the second 'for' is the link.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: kit or apparatus, as in camping or music equipment.

entries.clue: Prepare old crime boss for catastrophic conflict (10)

blocks.note: to arm is to prepare for fighting

annotation.surface: An elderly mob boss gets ready for a gang war.
annotation.walkthrough: The mafia surface fits the answer's world of violence, which hides where the definition begins.
annotation.definitionFit: Armageddon is the final great battle, any catastrophic conflict.

entries.clue: An urgent call about top-quality fireproofing (8)

indicators.note: the call goes about, around, the other word

annotation.surface: An emergency call about the finest fire safety.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a fire alarm about safety gear; 'about' is a container instruction, not 'concerning'.
annotation.definitionFit: Asbestos was used widely as fireproofing material.

entries.clue: Restricting crossing river is causing strain (6)

indicators.note: the word goes across the river, so R sits inside it

annotation.surface: Hemming in a river crossing puts pressure on it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Crossing' reads as a bridge over the river; it means the word straddles R.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: tiresome or taxing, as in a trying day.
